title: A high-throughput protocol for monitoring starvation-induced autophagy in real time in mouse embryonic fibroblasts
protocol: Conduct IncuCyte experiment.
Monitor turboGFP-LC3B signal in live cells upon starvation using an IncuCyte system.
Perform automated image acquisition and analysis through the IncuCyte software.
Adjust protocol for use with other high-throughput imaging platforms as needed.
Seed turboGFP-LC3B expressing cells into multi-well plates.
Trpysinize cells, inactivate trypsin with serum-containing medium and count cells using a method of choice.
Determine the appropriate number of cells to obtain 50%–70% confluence on the day of starvation for each cell type in a pilot experiment.
Seed MEFs at 12,000 cells per well in 24-well plates.
Allow cells to adhere overnight in the incubator.
Seed cells at the appropriate density without cell clusters.
Starve cells by removing medium.
Wash cells twice with warm PBS.
Wash cells once with starvation medium.
Add full (control) or starvation medium to the wells.
Place plate in available slot on IncuCyte and ensure secure seating.
Open IncuCyte software and select the appropriate plate type and imaging pattern.
Schedule scans every 2 or 4 hours for 2–5 days, selecting phase and green fluorescence channels.
Remove plate from scan schedule in IncuCyte software after completion of imaging period.
Remove plate from IncuCyte.
Generate processing definition timing: 45-60 minutes.
Train the software using selected images to determine optimal settings for automated object detection.
Define parameters for the phase contrast channel.
Adjust segmentation adjustment to 1.1 within the confluence mask.
Refine parameters by setting up Segmentation adjustment, which aims at adjusting the Background/Cells slider bar using a value of 1.1.
Adjust the size of the mask by reducing it by 1 pixel.
Exclude objects smaller than 200 μm² from the analysis.
Preview all images to ensure satisfaction with the segmentation parameters.
Set up top-hat processing for object segmentation in the green channel.
Define a fluorescence threshold of 2 GCU for the green channel.
Adjust edge sensitivity to optimize segmentation for adjacent objects.
Exclude objects smaller than 200 μm² in the green channel analysis.
Preview all images again to control and confirm the segmentation mask quality.
Launch the analysis after confirming satisfactory parameters.
Extract raw counts from IncuCyte software.
Export results for confluence percent calculations for phase contrast and green channels.
Copy raw data to an Excel file.
Calculate the ratio of percentage confluence in the green channel by the confluence in the phase contrast channel.
Label cell nuclei using a red probe if desired.
Normalize the number of fluorescent green objects by the number of nuclei when applicable.
Normalize obtained values with that of the first scan (time 0 h).
Import data into graphing software for analysis and visualization.
Generate a curve representing the levels of green fluorescence normalized by the number of cells.
Starve cells in EBSS supplemented with 10% serum and non-essential amino acids for the indicated times.
Measure fluorescent object confluence every 2 hours for up to 72 hours.
Divide fluorescent object confluence results by phase confluence results at the same time point.
Normalize the divided results with the first scan (0 h).
Perform immunoblotting of LC3B levels in MEFs starved for indicated times.
